title: Conjecture 1.1 (Gyárfás-Sumner Conjecture)
statement_text: For every forest $H$ there is a function $f$ such that $\chi(G) \leq f(\omega(G))$ for every $H$-free graph $G$.
context_text: The Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture is the central motivating problem of the paper. The paper proves a related strengthening of the Kierstead-Penrice theorem (which covers the case $H$ a tree of radius two), giving polynomial bounds on chromatic number in terms of $\tau_d(G)$. Taking $t=1$ in the main result recovers a bound on $\chi(G)$ in terms of $\omega(G)$ (doubly-exponential, but much smaller than Kierstead-Penrice's).
paper_contribution: Proves that for every tree $H$ of radius two and every integer $d \geq 1$, there is a polynomial $f$ such that $\chi(G) \leq f(\tau_d(G))$ for every $H$-free graph $G$ (Theorem 1.6), which in particular yields a doubly-exponential bound on $\chi(G)$ in terms of $\omega(G)$ for $H$-free graphs when $H$ is a tree of radius two.
notes: Attributed via citations [8, 21] in the paper; [8] is Gyárfás and [21] is Sumner.
paper_title: Polynomial bounds for chromatic number. V. Excluding a tree of radius two and a complete multipartite graph

title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: For every forest $H$, there is a polynomial $f$ such that $\chi(G) \leq f(\omega(G))$ for every $H$-free graph $G$.
context_text: A graph $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$; $\omega(G)$ is the clique number. A class of graphs is hereditary if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs, and $\chi$-bounded if there is a function $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all its members. The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture asserts that for every forest $H$ the class of $H$-free graphs is $\chi$-bounded; Kierstead and Penrice proved it for trees of radius two. Esperet conjectured that every $\chi$-bounded hereditary class admits a polynomial bounding function $f$; this has been disproved in general but remains open for classes excluding a forest, where together with Gyárfás–Sumner it gives the present conjecture. It is known only for a few classes of trees. The authors note that a polynomial bound for the five-vertex path $P_5$ (whose best known bound is $\omega^{\log_2\omega}$) would imply the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for $P_5$. Rödl proved that for every forest $H$, $H$-free graphs with no $K_{t,t}$ subgraph have bounded chromatic number, and the authors (with Spirkl) showed this bound can be taken polynomial in $t$, a special case of this conjecture.
notes: Stated in the paper without a parenthesised attribution; it is a natural combination of Conjecture 1.1 and Esperet's conjecture restricted to forest-free classes.
paper_title: Polynomial bounds for chromatic number. V. Excluding a tree of radius two and a complete multipartite graph

title: Question: Extending Theorem 1.6 to paths
statement_text: Is it true that if $H$ is a path, then for every integer $d \geq 1$, there is a polynomial $f$ such that $\chi(G) \leq f(\tau_d(G))$ for every $H$-free graph $G$?
context_text: A graph $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$; $\omega(G)$ is the clique number. A class of graphs is hereditary if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs, and $\chi$-bounded if there is a function $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all its members. For an integer $d\ge1$, $\tau_d(G)$ is the largest $t$ such that $G$ has a subgraph (not necessarily induced) isomorphic to the complete $d$-partite graph with every part of size $t$; thus $\tau_1(G)=|G|$, $\tau_2(G)$ is the largest $t$ with $K_{t,t}\subseteq G$, and $\tau_d(G)\ge\lfloor\omega(G)/d\rfloor$. Rödl proved that for every forest $H$ there is a function $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\tau_2(G))$ for every $H$-free $G$; for $H$ a path, a polynomial $f$ was obtained by Bonamy, Bousquet, Pilipczuk, Rzążewski, Thomassé and Walczak, and the authors (with Spirkl) proved it for every forest. The main result of the paper is that for every tree $H$ of radius two and every integer $d\ge1$ there is a polynomial $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\tau_d(G))$ for every $H$-free graph $G$ (a strengthening of the Kierstead–Penrice theorem). A referee suggested this question, extending that result to paths, another family of trees known to satisfy the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture (that $H$-free graphs are $\chi$-bounded for every forest $H$). Proving such a statement for a forest $H$ and all $d$ would imply that $H$ satisfies the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture.
notes: Explicitly labelled as an open question suggested by a referee and incorporated into the paper.
paper_title: Polynomial bounds for chromatic number. V. Excluding a tree of radius two and a complete multipartite graph

title: Question: Polynomial bound analogue of Esperet's conjecture for $\tau_d$
statement_text: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a hereditary class of graphs, and $d \geq 1$. Suppose that there is a function $f$ such that $\chi(G) \leq f(\tau_d(G))$ for each $G \in \mathcal{C}$. Can we always choose $f$ to be a polynomial? What if $d = 2$?
context_text: A graph $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$; $\omega(G)$ is the clique number. A class of graphs is hereditary if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs, and $\chi$-bounded if there is a function $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all its members. For an integer $d\ge1$, $\tau_d(G)$ is the largest $t$ such that $G$ has a subgraph (not necessarily induced) isomorphic to the complete $d$-partite graph with every part of size $t$; thus $\tau_1(G)=|G|$, $\tau_2(G)$ is the largest $t$ with $K_{t,t}\subseteq G$, and $\tau_d(G)\ge\lfloor\omega(G)/d\rfloor$. Esperet conjectured that every $\chi$-bounded hereditary class has a polynomial bounding function; this was disproved in general (Briański, Davies and Walczak) but remains open for classes excluding a forest. A referee suggested this analogue for $\tau_d$ in place of $\omega$. It is motivated by the paper's main result: for every tree $H$ of radius two and every integer $d\ge1$ there is a polynomial $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\tau_d(G))$ for every $H$-free graph $G$, and by the earlier result of the authors with Spirkl that for every forest $H$ there is $c>0$ with $\chi(G)\le\tau_2(G)^c$ for every $H$-free $G$.
notes: Explicitly labelled as an open question suggested by a referee and incorporated into the paper.
